title: El aumento
goal: Be told the rent is going up, and negotiate
culture: She is not a company and there is no contract to point at, which cuts both ways: she can raise it whenever she likes and she can also just decide not to. Es mucho said plainly, and a number in the middle, is the whole of the negotiation.

beats.es: Mi hijo, fíjese que el alquiler va a subir.
beats.en: It’s going up? By how much?
beats.good: Va a subir — it is going up. Ask the number before you say anything else, because the number is the only part that is negotiable.
The date is worth as much as the number. A rise next month and a rise today are two different conversations.

beats.objective: Say it is a lot — and stop
beats.good: Es mucho, said flatly and then nothing. She is not a company, and she may not have thought about it from your side until you said it out loud.

beats.en: Let’s settle on a hundred and fifteen.
beats.good: Quedemos en — let’s settle on. The same move as the leather bag in the market, and it works here for exactly the same reason.
